title: Dual Elimination Shutdown: Rivaroxaban + Ketoconazole in Moderate Renal Impairment

clinical_context.patient: 74-year-old female with non-valvular atrial fibrillation maintained on Rivaroxaban 15 mg once daily.
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Ketoconazole 200 mg PO once daily for severe chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Ketoconazole is substituted with Fluconazole 200 mg daily (a moderate CYP3A4 and weak P-gp inhibitor), does the absolute contraindication persist?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Prescribing Information Xarelto (rivaroxaban), Section 7.1 & 7.2
evidence_references.quote: Avoid concomitant administration of Xarelto with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir). Co-administration results in a 158% increase in mean AUC and 22% increase in Cmax.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Moderate renal impairment (CrCl 41 mL/min) already reduces baseline active renal tubular clearance by ~40%. Dual inhibition of hepatic CYP3A4 (~67% clearance) and renal P-gp/BCRP (~33% clearance) causes catastrophic accumulation (>2.6-fold AUC).
ground_truth.mandated_action: Avoid concomitant use per FDA Section 7.1/7.2. Do not attempt dose reduction.

counterfactual.explanation: Fluconazole is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and does not strongly inhibit P-gp. The combination is not absolutely contraindicated, but in CrCl <50 mL/min, rivaroxaban exposure still increases (~1.4x), requiring heightened clinical bleeding surveillance.

minimal_pairs.description: CrCl 41 mL/min vs CrCl 90 mL/min — action invariant, mechanism graph changes
minimal_pairs.explanation: Ketoconazole is a combined strong CYP3A4 + P-gp inhibitor. FDA label says 'avoid concomitant use' regardless of renal function. The action is invariant. However, the mechanism graph changes: at CrCl 90, the renal P-gp/BCRP backup pathway is intact (edge present), while at CrCl 41 that edge is lost. The model must preserve the action while correctly showing the mechanism graph difference.

title: Prodrug Bioactivation Defeat: Clopidogrel + Omeprazole with Unknown CYP2C19 Genotype

clinical_context.patient: 64-year-old male Day 14 post-PCI with drug-eluting stent on DAPT (Aspirin 81 mg daily + Clopidogrel 75 mg daily).

physiological_modifiers.platelet_function: Baseline post-PCI VerifyNow PRU 170 (therapeutic platelet inhibition)

clinical_context.acute_prescription: Omeprazole 40 mg PO daily for acute erosive reflux esophagitis.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Omeprazole is replaced with Pantoprazole 40 mg daily, explain the pharmacological basis for whether active metabolite formation is preserved.

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Plavix (clopidogrel) Boxed Warning & Section 7.1
evidence_references.quote: Avoid concomitant use of Plavix with omeprazole or esomeprazole. Omeprazole significantly reduces the antiplatelet activity of Plavix, reducing active thiol metabolite AUC by 45% (Day 1) and 40% (Day 5).

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Unknown CYP2C19 genotype does not equal poor metabolizer status. In patients with unknown status, intermediate (*1/*2) or poor (*2/*2) metabolizers may have compromised bioactivation. Omeprazole suicide inhibition substantially increases the probability of subtherapeutic active thiol metabolite and high on-treatment platelet reactivity. CPIC recommends genotyping; if unknown, consider alternative P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel/ticagrelor) or PPI switch.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Avoid concomitant use. Switch acid suppression to Pantoprazole or H2-receptor antagonist, or switch P2Y12 inhibitor to Prasugrel/Ticagrelor if clinically indicated.
fatal_traps: take omeprazole at bedtime and clopidogrel in morning

counterfactual.explanation: Pantoprazole exhibits significantly lower affinity for CYP2C19 and is metabolized primarily through cytosolic sulfotransferase, preserving clopidogrel bioactivation.

title: Electrolyte-Gated Proarrhythmic Cascade: Sotalol + HCTZ + Levofloxacin

clinical_context.patient: 68-year-old male with persistent atrial flutter on Sotalol 80 mg BID and Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) 25 mg daily.
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Levofloxacin 500 mg PO once daily for community-acquired pneumonia.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Levofloxacin is replaced with Doxycycline 100 mg BID (which lacks hERG blockade liability), is the proarrhythmic risk resolved while the patient remains hypokalemic?

evidence_references.citation: CredibleMeds Known Risk of TdP; FDA Betapace Prescribing Information §5.1
evidence_references.quote: Hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia should be corrected prior to initiation of Betapace. QTc interval increases in a dose-dependent manner. Both Sotalol and Levofloxacin produce concentration-dependent blockade of the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current (IKr).

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: HCTZ-induced hypokalemia (3.1 mEq/L) and hypomagnesemia (1.4 mg/dL) destabilize the hERG selectivity filter and increase channel drug-binding affinity, severely depleting cardiac repolarization reserve.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Avoid Levofloxacin. Urgent IV/oral potassium and magnesium repletion and telemetry monitoring required prior to antimicrobial therapy.
fatal_traps: safe to administer with ecg monitoring alone
doxycycline completely eliminates all cardiac risk

counterfactual.explanation: Replacing Levofloxacin with Doxycycline eliminates the antimicrobial hERG blocking component, but the residual risk remains HIGH and lethal because Sotalol + uncorrected hypokalemia (3.1 mEq/L) independently precipitates Torsades de Pointes.

minimal_pairs.description: K+ 3.1 mEq/L vs 4.5 mEq/L — residual risk persists even after antibiotic swap
minimal_pairs.explanation: Sotalol alone carries dose-dependent TdP risk; 'safe' is never correct at K+ 4.5. The correct state after Levofloxacin→Doxycycline swap is 'risk reduced, baseline Sotalol QT monitoring remains, Doxycycline is a non-QT-prolonging alternative.' The swap eliminates fluoroquinolone hERG block, but Sotalol dose-dependent hERG block persists. Grade on invariants: hypokalemia must be corrected, residual risk persists.

title: Renal Transporter Secretion Blockade: Methotrexate + Naproxen in Borderline Clearance

clinical_context.patient: 58-year-old female with severe rheumatoid arthritis maintained on weekly oral Methotrexate 15 mg and Folic Acid 1 mg daily.

physiological_modifiers.hydration_status: Mildly dehydrated from acute febrile illness

clinical_context.acute_prescription: Naproxen 500 mg PO BID prescribed for acute musculoskeletal pain.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Naproxen is substituted with Acetaminophen 650 mg TID, does the active renal tubular secretion inhibition persist?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Trexall (methotrexate) Prescribing Information, Section 5.1 & Section 7
evidence_references.quote: Severe, and some fatal, cases of bone marrow suppression and aplastic anemia have been reported with concomitant administration of methotrexate along with NSAIDs. NSAIDs competitively inhibit renal tubular secretion via OAT1/OAT3 and reduce renal perfusion.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Methotrexate is cleared predominantly (>80%) via active proximal renal tubular secretion mediated by OAT1 and OAT3. Naproxen competitively blocks OAT1/OAT3 and reduces renal prostaglandin synthesis, causing profound methotrexate accumulation, pancytopenia, and severe mucositis. Risk is highest with high-dose oncology methotrexate, dehydration, and impaired kidney function; low-dose weekly rheumatology methotrexate (15 mg/week) with normal renal function carries lower but non-zero risk.
ground_truth.mandated_action: High-risk context (dehydration, CrCl 48): discontinue naproxen, hydrate, use acetaminophen; monitor CBC, creatinine, MTX levels. In stable low-dose rheumatology MTX with normal renal function: enhanced monitoring may suffice.
fatal_traps: safe to take together if separated by 4 hours
no interaction between oral weekly methotrexate and nsaids

counterfactual.explanation: Acetaminophen does not inhibit organic anion transporters OAT1 or OAT3 and does not impair renal prostaglandin-mediated perfusion, completely resolving the pharmacokinetic clearance blockade.

minimal_pairs.description: High-dose oncology MTX + dehydration + CKD vs low-dose rheumatology MTX + normal renal
minimal_pairs.explanation: High-dose oncology MTX with dehydration and CKD is contraindicated with NSAIDs. Stable low-dose rheumatology MTX (7.5-15 mg/week) with normal renal function and euvolemia is co-prescribed with NSAIDs routinely with CBC/creatinine monitoring. A model that over-flags the rheumatology case as contraindicated should be graded as OVER_FLAGGING. The pair tests whether the model distinguishes dose/context appropriately.

title: Substrate Competition & Regulatory Dose Ceiling: Simvastatin + Amlodipine

clinical_context.patient: 62-year-old male with hyperlipidemia and newly uncontrolled Stage 2 hypertension, currently taking Simvastatin 40 mg PO nightly.
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Amlodipine 10 mg PO once daily added for blood pressure management.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: Can Simvastatin be maintained at 40 mg? If not, what is the exact maximum FDA-approved dose with Amlodipine, or what class-matched statin completely bypasses CYP3A4 competition?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Drug Safety Communication (June 2011) & Simvastatin Prescribing Information §2.2
evidence_references.quote: Do not exceed 20 mg simvastatin daily with concomitant amlodipine. Amlodipine increases systemic exposure of simvastatin acid by approximately 1.6-fold, significantly elevating the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Simvastatin is extensively cleared via first-pass CYP3A4 metabolism. Amlodipine moderately inhibits CYP3A4, elevating simvastatin lactone and active acid exposure by ~60%-70%, raising creatine kinase and rhabdomyolysis risk.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Reduce Simvastatin dose to a maximum ceiling of 20 mg daily, or switch to Rosuvastatin/Pravastatin.
fatal_traps: safe at 40 mg if taken with water

counterfactual.explanation: Reducing Simvastatin to 20 mg complies with the FDA safety ceiling. Alternatively, switching to Rosuvastatin completely resolves the interaction because Rosuvastatin undergoes minimal CYP metabolism (<10% via CYP2C9) and does not rely on CYP3A4.

title: CYP3A4/5 Multi-Enzyme Collapse: Tacrolimus + Voriconazole with CYP3A5*3/*3 Genotype

clinical_context.patient: 45-year-old male 6 months post-allogeneic renal transplant on Tacrolimus 4 mg BID (stable 12-hour trough level 7.5 ng/mL).

physiological_modifiers.graft_function: Serum creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, baseline eGFR 68 mL/min

clinical_context.acute_prescription: Voriconazole 200 mg PO BID initiated for pulmonary aspergillosis.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Tacrolimus dose is maintained unchanged, what occurs to whole-blood trough levels within 48 hours, and what is the mandated FDA starting empiric dose reduction?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Prograf (tacrolimus) §7.1 and Vfend (voriconazole) Prescribing Information §7.1
evidence_references.quote: When initiating voriconazole in patients currently on tacrolimus, reduce the tacrolimus dose to one-third (33%) of the original dose and monitor tacrolimus whole blood trough concentrations frequently due to a 3- to 6-fold increase in tacrolimus exposure.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Tacrolimus relies entirely on CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 for intestinal and hepatic elimination. Voriconazole is a potent dual inhibitor. In CYP3A5*3/*3 non-expressors, baseline clearance is already lower; Voriconazole induces a 300%-500% surge in trough concentrations, precipitating acute calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity, tremors, and graft injury. In CYP3A5*3/*3 non-expressors, CYP3A5 is non-functional, so the CYP3A5 inhibition edge is ABSENT — the multi-enzyme collapse is solely via CYP3A4.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Empirically reduce Tacrolimus dose by 66% to one-third (33%) of original dose immediately upon starting Voriconazole. Mandate serial whole-blood trough monitoring on days 1, 3, and 5.

counterfactual.explanation: Dose reduction to one-third prevents catastrophic overexposure, but residual risk remains HIGH requiring mandatory continuous therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) because inter-individual azole bioavailability is highly erratic.

minimal_pairs.description: CYP3A5*3/*3 (non-expressor) vs CYP3A5*1/*1 (expressor) — CYP3A5 edge flips, action invariant
minimal_pairs.explanation: In CYP3A5*3/*3 non-expressors, there is NO functional CYP3A5, so the Voriconazole→CYP3A5 inhibition edge is ABSENT (moot). In expressors, that edge IS PRESENT and contributes to the multi-enzyme collapse. The tacrolimus dose-reduction guidance (empiric 66% reduction) is the SAME regardless of genotype. This pair tests whether the model correctly shows the CYP3A5 edge flipping while keeping the regulatory action invariant.

title: Stereoselective Enantiomeric Clearance Blockade: Warfarin + Metronidazole

clinical_context.patient: 70-year-old male with mechanical mitral valve on chronic Warfarin 5 mg daily (stable INR 2.5).
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Metronidazole 500 mg PO TID prescribed for acute bacterial vaginosis / pelvic infection.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: Does Metronidazole inhibit the clearance of R-warfarin via CYP1A2/CYP3A4, or S-warfarin via CYP2C9? Explain the clinical consequence of this stereoselective distinction.

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Coumadin (warfarin sodium) Prescribing Information §7 & Flagyl §7.1
evidence_references.quote: Metronidazole selectively inhibits the metabolism of the S-enantiomer of warfarin by inhibiting CYP2C9, prolonging prothrombin time and significantly increasing INR and bleeding risk.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Commercial warfarin is a racemate. S-warfarin is 3 to 5 times more potent than R-warfarin at inhibiting vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1). Metronidazole stereoselectively inhibits CYP2C9 (the primary pathway for S-warfarin clearance), resulting in significant INR elevation typically within 3-5 days; magnitude varies by patient factors. R-warfarin clearance via CYP1A2/3A4 may also be inhibited by metronidazole at high doses.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Empirically reduce Warfarin dose by 30% to 50% upon starting Metronidazole. Check INR within 48 to 72 hours.
fatal_traps: safe to continue without inr monitoring

counterfactual.explanation: If alternative non-interacting antibiotics (e.g., Clindamycin or Amoxicillin-Clavulanate depending on indication) are used, stereoselective CYP2C9 inhibition is bypassed, but underlying infection and diet changes still require standard INR vigilance.

minimal_pairs.explanation: Non-interacting antibiotics bypass stereoselective CYP2C9 inhibition entirely.

title: Renal Proximal Tubule Sodium-Mimic Synergy: Lithium + Lisinopril + Furosemide

clinical_context.patient: 52-year-old female with Bipolar I disorder maintained on stable Lithium Carbonate 600 mg PO BID (steady-state serum lithium 0.85 mEq/L).

physiological_modifiers.new_comorbidity: Newly diagnosed congestive heart failure with peripheral edema

clinical_context.acute_prescription: Furosemide 40 mg PO daily and Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily initiated simultaneously.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: Trace how loop-diuretic sodium loss alters proximal tubule lithium reabsorption, and explain why adding an ACE inhibitor converts a moderate risk into acute severe neurotoxicity.

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Lithobid / Eskalith Prescribing Info §7 and Zestril (lisinopril) Label §7.4
evidence_references.quote: Lithium toxicity has been reported in patients receiving lithium concomitantly with drugs which cause elimination of sodium, including loop/thiazide diuretics and ACE inhibitors. Concomitant administration requires frequent serum lithium determinations.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Thiazide diuretics are the canonical high-confidence lithium interaction; loop diuretic (furosemide) effects are less uniform and strongly volume-status dependent. Furosemide blocks Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransport in the thick ascending limb, causing volume contraction and hyponatremia (Na+ 132 mEq/L). The kidney compensates by upregulating proximal tubule sodium reabsorption. Because Li+ is a monovalent cation with similar ionic radius, proximal tubules reabsorb Li+ indiscriminately. Lisinopril dilates efferent renal arterioles, reducing GFR and trapping accumulated Lithium. ACE inhibitors independently reduce GFR and lithium clearance. The triple combination is highest risk.
ground_truth.mandated_action: High toxicity hazard. Reduce Lithium dose by 50% proactively, or avoid the triple combination; check serum lithium levels and renal function within 48-72 hours.
fatal_traps: safe to add both medications without lithium dose reduction
lithium is metabolized by liver enzymes cyp3a4

counterfactual.explanation: Even if Furosemide is dose-titrated or switched, Lisinopril independently reduces GFR and causes chronic lithium retention, meaning frequent therapeutic drug monitoring remains strictly mandatory.

minimal_pairs.explanation: Lisinopril alone still reduces GFR and causes lithium retention; furosemide adds proximal tubule reabsorption synergy but is not the sole driver.

title: Safe Combination Control: Atorvastatin + Azithromycin (No Clinically Meaningful CYP3A4 Inhibition)

clinical_context.patient: 55-year-old male with hyperlipidemia on Atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly.
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1, then 250 mg daily days 2-5 for acute bacterial sinusitis.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Azithromycin is substituted with Clarithromycin 500 mg BID (a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor), would the interaction profile change?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Lipitor (atorvastatin) Prescribing Information Section 7.1 & 12.3
evidence_references.quote: Azithromycin does not inhibit CYP3A4 and does not significantly increase atorvastatin exposure. Co-administration of atorvastatin with azithromycin does not require dose adjustment. In contrast, strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole) increase atorvastatin AUC by up to 4-fold.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Azithromycin is a macrolide antibiotic that lacks the N-demethylated tertiary amine structure responsible for CYP3A4 inhibition seen in clarithromycin and erythromycin. It does not form a metabolic intermediate complex with CYP3A4 heme iron. This is a 'no clinically meaningful CYP3A4 inhibition at standard doses' control. NOTE: Azithromycin carries QT prolongation/TdP risk in patients with hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or on antiarrhythmics; this is a CYP3A4-PK negative control ONLY, not an overall safety endorsement.
ground_truth.mandated_action: No dose adjustment required. Atorvastatin 40 mg may be continued with azithromycin. Monitor CK if symptoms develop.
fatal_traps: azithromycin is completely safe in all patients

counterfactual.explanation: Clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and would increase atorvastatin AUC ~4-fold, requiring dose reduction or alternative antibiotic. This contrast validates that the benchmark correctly distinguishes safe macrolides from interacting ones.

title: Safe Combination Control: Warfarin + Ceftriaxone (No CYP-Mediated PK Interaction)

clinical_context.patient: 68-year-old female with mechanical aortic valve on chronic Warfarin 4 mg daily (stable INR 2.8).
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily for community-acquired pneumonia (hospitalized).
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Ceftriaxone is substituted with Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) DS BID, how does the interaction mechanism differ?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Coumadin Prescribing Information Section 7 & Clinical Pharmacology Literature
evidence_references.quote: Third-generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone, cefotaxime) lack significant CYP2C9 inhibitory activity and do not displace warfarin from albumin. They may transiently reduce vitamin K-producing gut flora, but the effect on INR is clinically negligible in patients with normal nutrition. In contrast, TMP-SMX is a potent CYP2C9 inhibitor and displaces warfarin from protein binding, increasing S-warfarin AUC by 30-50%.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: Ceftriaxone reduces vitamin K-producing gut flora, especially in hospitalized patients with poor oral intake. This can cause INR elevation of 0.5-1.5 units within 3-5 days. The effect is not CYP-mediated (ceftriaxone does not inhibit CYP2C9 or displace warfarin from albumin) but is a pharmacodynamic interaction via vitamin K depletion. In frail/malnourished inpatients, warfarin dose reduction of 10-20% may be needed with INR monitoring at 48-72h. This is a 'no CYP PK interaction' control that still requires clinical monitoring — distinct from TMP-SMX which has dual CYP2C9 inhibition + protein displacement.
ground_truth.mandated_action: No empiric warfarin dose reduction for CYP interaction. Check INR at 48-72h after ceftriaxone initiation in hospitalized patients. Reduce warfarin 10-20% if INR >3.5. Continue standard weekly INR monitoring. Do not withhold ceftriaxone for fear of CYP-mediated interaction.
fatal_traps: reduce warfarin dose empirically for CYP interaction

counterfactual.explanation: TMP-SMX would require ~30-50% warfarin reduction and INR check at 48-72 hours due to dual CYP2C9 inhibition and protein displacement. Even with ceftriaxone substitution, residual INR drift from vitamin K flora depletion may persist in frail/malnourished patients, requiring monitoring. The contrast proves models must distinguish cephalosporin safety (no CYP PK interaction) from sulfonamide danger (CYP + protein binding).

title: Pharmacogenomic Crisis: Codeine + CYP2D6 Ultrarapid Metabolizer

clinical_context.patient: 8-year-old post-tonsillectomy (weight 28 kg), prescribed Codeine 30 mg PO q6h PRN pain.
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Codeine 30 mg PO q6h as needed for post-operative pain.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Codeine is replaced with Morphine 2.5 mg PO q4h, does the life-threatening respiratory depression risk resolve?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Codeine Boxed Warning (2013) & CPIC CYP2D6/Codeine Guideline
evidence_references.quote: Children with CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer phenotype convert codeine to morphine more rapidly and completely, leading to life-threatening respiratory depression and death. Codeine is contraindicated in children <12 years for post-tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy pain.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: CYP2D6 UM genotype (*1/*2xN) causes ultra-rapid conversion of codeine to morphine, producing toxic morphine levels in children. Respiratory depression occurs at standard doses. FDA contraindicates codeine for post-tonsillectomy pain in children <12 years.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Absolute contraindication. Avoid codeine entirely in CYP2D6 UM and children <12 years. Use non-opioid analgesics (acetaminophen/ibuprofen) or morphine with careful titration.

counterfactual.explanation: Morphine bypasses CYP2D6 bioactivation, eliminating the pharmacogenomic risk. However, standard opioid precautions (respiratory monitoring, dose titration) still apply.

clinical_context.patient: 32-year-old female with refractory Crohn's disease, initiated on Azathioprine 2.5 mg/kg/day.
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Azathioprine 150 mg PO daily (2.5 mg/kg) for Crohn's maintenance.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Azathioprine is switched to Methotrexate 15 mg weekly, does the myelosuppression risk resolve?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Imuran (azathioprine) Boxed Warning & CPIC TPMT/Thiopurine Guideline
evidence_references.quote: Patients with homozygous TPMT deficiency (*3A/*3A, *3C/*3C) are at extreme risk for severe, life-threatening myelosuppression from standard azathioprine doses. Reduce dose to 10% of standard and monitor CBC weekly, or avoid entirely.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: TPMT*3A/*3A homozygotes have <5% enzyme activity. Azathioprine is shunted toward toxic 6-thioguanine nucleotides (6-TGN), causing profound myelosuppression (neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia) within 2-4 weeks at standard doses. CPIC recommends 10% dose reduction or alternative therapy.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Reduce azathioprine to 10% of standard dose (0.25 mg/kg) with weekly CBC monitoring, OR avoid azathioprine and use alternative (methotrexate, biologics).

counterfactual.explanation: Methotrexate does not require TPMT for metabolism and bypasses the thiopurine toxicity pathway entirely. Standard methotrexate monitoring (CBC, LFTs) applies.

title: HLA-B*57:01 Hypersensitivity: Abacavir in HLA-B*57:01 Positive Patient

clinical_context.patient: 41-year-old male with newly diagnosed HIV, HLA-B*57:01 positive, initiated on Abacavir 300 mg BID as part of ART.
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Abacavir 300 mg PO BID + Lamivudine 300 mg + Dolutegravir 50 mg daily.
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Abacavir is replaced with Tenofovir Alafenamide 25 mg daily, does the hypersensitivity reaction risk resolve?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Ziagen (abacavir) Boxed Warning & CPIC HLA-B/Abacavir Guideline
evidence_references.quote: Abacavir is contraindicated in patients positive for HLA-B*57:01 allele. Hypersensitivity reaction occurs in ~50-60% of HLA-B*57:01 positive patients vs <1% negative. Re-exposure after reaction causes anaphylaxis and death.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: HLA-B*57:01 presents abacavir as an altered self-peptide, triggering massive CD8+ T-cell activation and systemic hypersensitivity (fever, rash, hepatitis, renal failure). Positive predictive value ~50-60%. FDA mandates HLA-B*57:01 screening before initiation; contraindicated if positive.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Absolute contraindication. Do not use abacavir in HLA-B*57:01 positive patients. Switch to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) based regimen.

counterfactual.explanation: Tenofovir alafenamide does not associate with HLA-B*57:01 hypersensitivity. Standard renal monitoring for tenofovir applies.

title: UGT1A1*28 Polymorphism: Irinotecan in Homozygous *28/*28 Patient

clinical_context.patient: 58-year-old male with metastatic colorectal cancer, UGT1A1*28/*28 homozygous, scheduled for FOLFIRI (Irinotecan 180 mg/m2 q2w).
clinical_context.acute_prescription: Irinotecan 180 mg/m2 IV day 1 of 14-day cycle (FOLFIRI regimen).
clinical_context.counterfactual_probe: If Irinotecan dose is reduced to 120 mg/m2 per CPIC guidelines, does the severe neutropenia risk resolve?

evidence_references.citation: US FDA Camptosar (irinotecan) Prescribing Information & CPIC UGT1A1/Irinotecan Guideline
evidence_references.quote: UGT1A1*28/*28 homozygotes have ~30% glucuronidation activity for SN-38 (active irinotecan metabolite). At standard doses, risk of Grade 4 neutropenia is ~50%. CPIC recommends 25-50% dose reduction for *28/*28.

ground_truth.physiological_modifier_impact: UGT1A1*28/*28 reduces SN-38 glucuronidation to ~30% of normal, causing SN-38 accumulation. This increases topoisomerase I inhibition in bone marrow, leading to severe neutropenia (Grade 3-4 in ~50% at standard dose). CPIC recommends 25-50% dose reduction.
ground_truth.mandated_action: Reduce irinotecan starting dose by at least 25-50% (to 120 mg/m2 or lower). Mandate pre-cycle CBC and G-CSF prophylaxis consideration. Do not use standard 180 mg/m2 dose.
fatal_traps: prophylactic antibiotics instead of dose reduction

counterfactual.explanation: Dose reduction to 120 mg/m2 significantly reduces but does not eliminate neutropenia risk in *28/*28. Residual risk requires continued CBC monitoring and G-CSF support. Alternative non-irinotecan regimens (FOLFOX) bypass UGT1A1 entirely.
